title: Changing an additional term's payment_type re-materializes its entire charge history under the new type (duplicate charges for every past period)
description: The charges idempotency key is UNIQUE (owner_id, tenancy_id, payment_type, period_key) (verified live: charges_owner_id_tenancy_id_payment_type_period_key_key), and materialize_due_charges builds the key as `'term:' || term.id || ':' || occurrence.period_key` with payment_type = term.payment_type (20260715011000.sql:47-49). updatePaymentTermSettings (src/api/billing.ts:238-241) lets the owner change payment_type on an existing term, and useBilling.updateAdditionalPayment (useBilling.ts:418-428) calls materializeDueCharges() right after. Because payment_type is part of the conflict target, none of the existing charges conflict any more — so `on conflict … do nothing` does nothing, and a full parallel set of charges is inserted.
failure_scenario: Owner has a 'ועד בית' (committee) fixed term of ₪150 running since seq 1, with 7 materialized+paid charges (period_keys term:<id>:schedule:gregorian:2026-01-05 … 2026-07-05, payment_type 'committee'). Owner opens the term settings and changes סוג התשלום from 'ועד בית' to 'גז' (gas) because it was mis-categorised. updatePaymentTermSettings sets payment_type='gas'; materialize_due_charges then inserts 7 NEW charges with payment_type 'gas' and the SAME period_keys — none of which conflict with the existing 'committee' rows. The tenant now owes ₪1,050 of unpaid 'גז' charges on top of the ₪1,050 of already-paid 'ועד בית' charges, for the same seven months.
suggested_fix: Either forbid changing payment_type on a term that already has charges, or make the charge conflict target (owner_id, tenancy_id, period_key) — period_key already contains the term id and is globally unique per term/period — and update payment_type/label in place when the term changes.

title: materialize_due_charges was re-created with SET search_path = public instead of the empty search_path used elsewhere
description: The original definition in 20260714213000_billing_schedules_and_history.sql:160 correctly used `set search_path = ''` and fully-qualified every object. The re-creation in 20260715011000_payment_terms_start_sequence.sql:8 changed it to `set search_path = public`, and the live catalog confirms the drift: pg_proc.proconfig for materialize_due_charges is `{search_path=public}` while save_tenancy_billing_schedule is `{search_path=""}`. For a SECURITY DEFINER function owned by postgres, a mutable schema on the search_path is the classic definer-hijack vector. It is not exploitable today only because nspacl for schema public grants no CREATE to anon or authenticated (`anon=U/pg_database_owner | authenticated=U/pg_database_owner` - USAGE only), so no attacker-controlled role can plant a shadowing function or operator in public. It is a hardening regression that removes the safety margin and is inconsistent with the other DEFINER function in the same feature.
failure_scenario: If any future migration grants CREATE on schema public to authenticated (a common convenience when adding user-defined helpers), a signed-in attacker creates public.mod(integer, integer) or a shadowing operator that is resolved ahead of pg_catalog's, and materialize_due_charges - running as postgres with RLS bypassed - executes it against every owner's billing_schedule_occurrences rows. With search_path = '' (as save_tenancy_billing_schedule uses) that resolution is impossible.
suggested_fix: Restore `set search_path = ''` on materialize_due_charges (every object reference in the body is already schema-qualified, so no other change is needed).

title: Correcting a charge downward silently deletes the tenant's real payment record and rewrites the paid amount
description: In saveUtilityCharge (useBilling.ts:342-348), saveMeterTermCharge (485-491) and saveFixedTermCharge (517-523) the pattern is: ensureCharge() upserts the charge with the NEW (lower) amount_due, then `if (existing && Number(existing.paid_amount) > amountDue) await setChargePaymentState({ charge_id: charge.id, amount_due: amountDue, paid_amount: amountDue })`. set_charge_payment_state (live definition, SECURITY INVOKER) does not adjust the existing ledger, it DESTROYS it: it loops every payment_allocation on the charge, deletes the allocation, and then `if v_payment_amount <= v_allocation.amount then delete from public.payments where id = v_allocation.payment_id` (i.e. deletes the payment row outright), before inserting a single fresh payment for p_paid_amount. So passing paid_amount = the reduced amount_due does not record a credit or an overpayment; it erases the difference from the database entirely. The DB cannot even represent the truth: set_charge_payment_state raises 23514 when p_paid_amount > p_amount_due, and PaymentHistoryDialog.tsx:24 clamps with Math.max(amount_due - paid_amount, 0). This violates the binding rule 'Partial payments must never be lost'.
failure_scenario: Alice records an electricity charge from a mistyped meter reading: previous=1000, current=2000, rate=0.5 => amount_due = 500. The tenant pays 500 in full, so the ledger holds payments(amount=500) and payment_allocations(amount=500) for that charge. Alice notices the current reading was really 1600 and re-opens the utility dialog, entering previous=1000, current=1600, rate=0.5 => amountDue = 300. saveUtilityCharge calls ensureCharge (amount_due -> 300), then sees existing.paid_amount (500) > 300 and calls setChargePaymentState(charge_id, amount_due=300, paid_amount=300). The RPC deletes the 500 payment row and its allocation and inserts a new payment of 300. The 200 the tenant actually paid is gone from the database with no trace; the app now shows 'שולם 300 מתוך 300' and no credit is carried to the next month. The tenant is billed 200 more than they owe over the life of the tenancy.
suggested_fix: Never silently clamp. Either (1) allow paid_amount > amount_due at the DB level and surface the overpayment as a credit, or (2) refuse the downward correction in the UI and require the owner to explicitly acknowledge the resulting refund/credit, recording it (e.g. a negative-amount charge or a credit row) rather than deleting the payment. In all cases set_charge_payment_state should reduce/adjust allocations rather than DELETE FROM payments.

title: Nothing enforces sum(allocations) <= charge.amount_due; a stale client cache is the only guard
description: ensureCharge()/ensureRentCharge() are plain PostgREST upserts of amount_due (RLS only). There is no DB constraint or trigger tying sum(payment_allocations.amount) to charges.amount_due (verified against pg_constraint: charges only has amount_due >= 0, payment_allocations only amount > 0). The only check is the client-side 'if (existing && Number(existing.paid_amount) > amountDue)' guard in useBilling, which reads paid_amount from the React Query cache — and the two operations (upsert charge, then RPC) are not atomic. If the cache is stale, or if the second call fails, the DB is left with allocations exceeding amount_due, and paid_amount is recomputed client-side in listCharges (src/api/billing.ts:65) so the UI happily renders the impossible state.
failure_scenario: Owner has the app open in two tabs. Tab A loaded the electricity charge when it was ₪800 / paid 0. In tab B the owner clicks 'סמן שולם' (allocations now total ₪800). Back in tab A (cache not refetched) the owner corrects the meter reading and clicks 'עדכן חיוב' with a new amount of ₪300: ensureCharge sets amount_due = 300, and the guard does not fire because tab A's cached paid_amount is 0. The DB now has amount_due 300 with ₪800 of allocations. PaymentsPage shows 'שולם ₪800 מתוך ₪300', the header tiles report totalPaid inflated by ₪500 against a totalDue of ₪300, and 'נשאר' is floor-clamped to 0 so the discrepancy is invisible. (Same end state if the network drops between the ensureCharge upsert and the setChargePaymentState clamp.)
suggested_fix: Move charge-amount edits into the same RPC as the payment state and add a DB-level invariant (trigger or constraint) that sum(payment_allocations.amount) per charge never exceeds charges.amount_due, and per payment never exceeds payments.amount.

title: greatest(p_schedule_start_date, current_date) rewrites schedule_start_date to the edit date, renumbering sequence_no on the next edit and moving every bi-monthly term to the wrong months
description: Line 112 stores `greatest(p_schedule_start_date, current_date)` — so every schedule edit made after the schedule started silently advances schedule_start_date to TODAY. BillingSettingsDialog.tsx:64 then re-uses `settings.schedule_start_date` as the startDate for the NEXT edit, and generateBillingSchedule numbers sequence_no from 1 relative to whatever startDate it is given (billingSchedule.ts:191, 230). So from the second edit onward the future occurrences are renumbered from 1 while the past occurrences keep their original numbers. tenancy_payment_terms.starts_on_sequence is an absolute sequence number and is never remapped, and materialize_due_charges keys bi-monthly billing off `mod(occurrence.sequence_no - term.starts_on_sequence, term.frequency_months) = 0` (20260715011000.sql:66). The anchor therefore lands on different calendar months after the renumbering, and sequence numbers become non-unique within a tenancy (no unique constraint on (owner_id, tenancy_id, sequence_no) — verified live), so occurrenceForFrequency (PaymentsPage.tsx:490-497) can match two different months for the same sequence_no.
failure_scenario: Schedule: gregorian, due_day 25, schedule_start_date 2026-01-05. Bi-monthly electricity term, frequency_months 2, starts_on_sequence 1 → bills on odd sequences = Jan, Mar, May, Jul, Sep, Nov. Edit #1 on 2026-07-14: owner changes due_day 25→5. schedule_start_date is silently stored as 2026-07-14. Occurrences inserted keep the old numbering (Aug = seq 8). Edit #2 on 2026-08-20 (owner switches the calendar to Hebrew, or nudges the day again). The dialog now passes startDate = 2026-07-14; generateBillingSchedule numbers the first due date on/after 2026-07-14 as seq 1 → 2026-08-05 = seq 1, 2026-09-05 = seq 2, 2026-10-05 = seq 3. The insert filter keeps everything >= 2026-08-20, so September lands in the DB as sequence_no 2 (it used to be 9). Electricity anchored on starts_on_sequence=1 with frequency 2 now bills on seq 1,3,5… = Aug, Oct, Dec — September's electricity is never billed, and October gets billed instead of an odd month. Separately, sequence_no 2 now exists twice for that tenancy (Feb 2026 and Sep 2026).
suggested_fix: Do not clamp schedule_start_date forward — store p_schedule_start_date as given (it is the sequence anchor), and use `greatest(...)` only for the delete/insert cut-off. Add a unique constraint on (owner_id, tenancy_id, sequence_no), which would have made this fail loudly instead of silently renumbering.

title: Backdating the schedule start date silently DELETES the entire billing schedule and inserts nothing — success toast, billing dead forever
description: save_tenancy_billing_schedule() unconditionally DELETEs every occurrence with due_date >= current_date (line 121-124), then re-INSERTs only the submitted occurrences whose due_date >= greatest(p_schedule_start_date, current_date) (line 143). The client (src/hooks/useBilling.ts:161-166) always generates exactly 48 occurrences starting AT p_schedule_start_date. So if the owner picks a start date more than 48 periods in the past, ALL 48 generated occurrences fall before current_date, the insert filter drops every single one, and the tenancy is left with zero future occurrences. The RPC returns void (no row count is checked anywhere), useBilling.saveBillingSettings toasts 'מועד התשלום נשמר', and the dialog closes. This is exactly the forbidden 'a failed operation looks like a successful one'. The Gregorian start-date input (src/components/BillingSettingsDialog.tsx:242-248, <Input type="date">) has no `min` attribute, and the field is literally labelled 'מתאריך' — backdating it to the lease start is the obvious thing an owner does.
failure_scenario: Today is 2026-07-14 (DB current_date, verified live). Tenancy has a working schedule (due_day 5, occurrences through 2030). Owner opens 'מועד תשלום' and sets מתאריך = 2022-05-01 to make the schedule match the original lease. Client generates 48 occurrences: 2022-05-05 … 2026-04-05. RPC: DELETE removes all 41 future occurrences (2026-08-05 … 2030-03-05); INSERT filter `due_date >= greatest('2022-05-01', '2026-07-14')` matches 0 of 48 rows (verified by live query: generated=48, would_insert=0). Result: billing_schedule_occurrences for that tenancy now contains only the handful of already-past rows. materialize_due_charges() has no occurrence to work from, so NO rent charge is ever created again for that tenant, for the rest of the tenancy. The UI shows a green 'מועד התשלום נשמר' toast and the settings dialog shows schedule_start_date = 2026-07-14 as if all is well.
suggested_fix: Reject the call when the number of rows actually inserted is 0 (or < some floor): capture `get diagnostics v_inserted = row_count` after the INSERT and `raise exception` if it is 0. Better: generate the occurrence window server-side from (schedule_start_date, today) so the count is always right, and/or clamp/validate p_schedule_start_date in the dialog (min = tenancy.start_date, and warn when the generated window ends in the past).

title: Changing due_day mid-tenancy skips a whole month — that month is never billed at all
description: The DELETE cuts at `due_date >= current_date` but the re-INSERT cuts at `due_date >= greatest(p_schedule_start_date, current_date)` — the same boundary. Any occurrence for the CURRENT month that (a) had an old due date on/after today and (b) has a new due date before today falls into the gap: the old row is deleted, the new row is filtered out, and no occurrence for that month survives. materialize_due_charges() only ever creates charges from occurrence rows, so that month produces no rent charge, ever. Nothing in the UI or the RPC reports this.
failure_scenario: Tenancy: rent ₪5,000, gregorian, due_day 25, schedule_start_date 2026-01-05. Occurrences: 2026-01-25 (seq 1) … 2026-07-25 (seq 7) … On 2026-07-14 the owner changes יום בחודש from 25 to 5. Client regenerates from 2026-01-05 with dueDay 5 → seq 7 = 2026-07-05. RPC: DELETE removes 2026-07-25 (>= 2026-07-14); INSERT keeps only due_date >= greatest(2026-01-05, 2026-07-14) = 2026-07-14, so 2026-07-05 is dropped. July 2026 now has ZERO occurrences. The cron runs every night and never emits a July rent charge. The owner loses ₪5,000 of billing for July and there is no error, no warning, and no visible gap in the UI (PaymentsPage just shows June as 'מועד חיוב' and August as 'מועד הבא').
suggested_fix: Delete/insert on the same PERIOD boundary, not the same date boundary: compute the current period (the occurrence whose period contains today) and rebuild from the NEXT period onward, leaving the current period's row untouched. Or key occurrences by period (year+month / hebrew year+month) rather than by due date so the current period's row is UPDATEd in place instead of deleted-and-dropped.

title: Changing an existing term's payment type re-materializes DUPLICATE charges for every past period
description: updateAdditionalPayment() calls updatePaymentTermSettings() (which writes tenancy_payment_terms.payment_type straight from the client — AddAdditionalPaymentDialog.tsx:157-166 renders the type <select> in edit mode too) and then immediately calls materializeDueCharges(). materialize_due_charges inserts term charges with period_key 'term:<term_id>:<period>' and relies on 'on conflict (owner_id, tenancy_id, payment_type, period_key) do nothing'. payment_type is part of that conflict key, so after the type changes the already-materialized charges no longer collide: a second charge is created for every past-due occurrence, at the term's CURRENT fixed_amount. The old charges (including fully paid ones) stay. charges has no FK to the term, so nothing links or dedupes them.
failure_scenario: Term 'ועד בית' (payment_type='committee', fixed ₪300, starts_on_sequence=1) has been billing for 6 months; 4 of the 6 charges are paid. Owner opens the term's edit dialog to rename it and changes 'סוג התשלום' from 'ועד בית' to 'אחר' (custom). On save, materialize_due_charges inserts 6 NEW charges (payment_type='custom', same period_keys, ₪300 each, paid_amount 0). Total due on PaymentsPage jumps by ₪1,800 of debt that does not exist, PaymentHistoryDialog shows two identical rows for every month, and the 4 months the tenant already paid now display an unpaid duplicate.
suggested_fix: Give charges a real term_id FK (composite with owner_id) and make it part of the uniqueness key instead of payment_type, or forbid changing payment_type once charges exist for the term.

title: Deleting a payment term silently erases every recorded payment made against it; the confirmation text does not say so
description: The confirm dialog says 'הפעולה תמחק את התשלום הנוסף ואת החיובים שנוצרו ממנו. אי אפשר לבטל את המחיקה.' The live SECURITY DEFINER function `delete_added_payment_term` (verified via pg_get_functiondef) does far more than that: it iterates every payment_allocation whose charge period_key matches `term:<id>:%`, deletes the allocation, and then DELETES the payments row outright (or decrements it). So money the owner already collected and recorded disappears from the payments ledger, not just the charges. The dialog never mentions payments or 'תשלומים שכבר נרשמו', so the owner cannot know that clicking 'מחק תשלום' destroys a year of receipt history.
failure_scenario: Owner added a 'גז' term in January; over 8 months he recorded ₪200/month collected — ₪1,600 of payments. In September the tenant switches to a gas company that bills directly, so the owner clicks the trash icon on the גז card to stop future billing. The dialog only warns about 'החיובים שנוצרו ממנו'. He confirms. All 8 charges AND all 8 payments rows are deleted: the 'שולם' total in היסטוריית תשלומים drops by ₪1,600 and every record that the tenant ever paid gas is gone, with no undo.
suggested_fix: Either archive the term instead of hard-deleting (the table already has archived_at and listPaymentTerms filters on it), or spell out in the AlertDialogDescription that all recorded payments for this term (₪X across N חיובים) will be deleted permanently, showing the actual paid total.

title: revoke all ... from public is a no-op: anon holds EXECUTE on every phase-2 RPC, including both SECURITY DEFINER ones
description: Both phase-2 migrations end each SECURITY DEFINER function with the pair `revoke all on function ... from public;` + `grant execute on function ... to authenticated;` (lines 153-154 and 226-227 of 20260714213000_billing_schedules_and_history.sql, and lines 77-78 of 20260715011000_payment_terms_start_sequence.sql). The author's clear intent is that only signed-in users can call these RPCs. The revoke does nothing. Supabase ships ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA public GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTIONS TO anon, authenticated, service_role for role postgres. I confirmed it in pg_default_acl: for defaclobjtype='f', schema public, grantor postgres, the ACL is `postgres=X/postgres | anon=X/postgres | authenticated=X/postgres | service_role=X/postgres`. That is an EXPLICIT grant to the anon ROLE, not a grant to the PUBLIC pseudo-role. REVOKE ... FROM PUBLIC strips only the PUBLIC entry and leaves the explicit anon=X entry intact. Live proof: pg_proc.proacl for materialize_due_charges and save_tenancy_billing_schedule is `postgres=X/postgres | anon=X/postgres | authenticated=X/postgres | service_role=X/postgres`, and has_function_privilege('anon', oid, 'EXECUTE') returns TRUE for materialize_due_charges, save_tenancy_billing_schedule, set_charge_payment_state and delete_added_payment_term (correctly FALSE for rls_auto_enable, which was never granted). get_advisors(security) independently flags anon_security_definer_function_executable on both DEFINER functions. This is the ROOT CAUSE behind known bug (a) and is distinct from it: an anonymous caller only ever reaches the `(v_owner_id is null or ...)` clause because the revoke that was supposed to keep anon out is dead code. Patching that one WHERE clause therefore fixes the symptom while leaving the entire public schema's SECURITY DEFINER surface anon-callable, so the next DEFINER function added with the same boilerplate is exposed again by default. The correct statement is `revoke all on function ... from anon;` (or `from anon, public;`).
failure_scenario: With only the project's publishable anon key and NO Authorization header, POST to https://<project-ref>.supabase.co/rest/v1/rpc/materialize_due_charges with headers `apikey: <anon key>` and `Content-Type: application/json`, body `{}`. PostgREST authenticates the request as role `anon`; has_function_privilege('anon', 'public.materialize_due_charges()', 'EXECUTE') is true, so the call is NOT rejected with 42501 and instead executes as SECURITY DEFINER with auth.uid() = NULL. Same for /rest/v1/rpc/save_tenancy_billing_schedule. Any unauthenticated visitor to the deployed site can invoke the app's privileged RPCs.
suggested_fix: Replace `revoke all on function public.materialize_due_charges() from public;` with `revoke all on function public.materialize_due_charges() from public, anon;` and do the same for save_tenancy_billing_schedule, set_charge_payment_state and delete_added_payment_term. Then re-assert with has_function_privilege('anon', ...) = false and add an anon-client test (see the test-coverage finding).

title: The money schema and its RPCs have no migration files in the repo
description: supabase_migrations.schema_migrations on the live project lists 16 applied migrations, but supabase/migrations/ contains only 3 .sql files (glob of the whole repo confirms there are no others). Missing from the repo are, among others, billing_mvp_charges_payments (the charges / payments / payment_allocations tables), set_charge_payment_state, fix_set_charge_payment_state_zero, tenancy_payment_terms and delete_added_payment_term. The two functions that mutate money (set_charge_payment_state, delete_added_payment_term) exist only inside the dev database — their source is not in version control, was never diffable, and cannot be reviewed or re-applied.
failure_scenario: Deploying phase 2 to a fresh (production) project: `supabase db push` applies only the 3 committed files. 20260714213000_billing_schedules_and_history.sql references public.charges and public.tenancies, so the push fails outright; if it is force-ordered, the resulting database has no charges/payments/payment_allocations tables and no set_charge_payment_state or delete_added_payment_term, so every 'סמן שולם' and every term deletion fails with 'function does not exist'. Equally, if the dev project is reset, the definitions of the two money-mutating functions are permanently lost.
suggested_fix: Dump the 5 unversioned migrations out of the live project into supabase/migrations/ so the full ledger schema and both money RPCs are reproducible and reviewable from the repo.

title: starts_on_sequence defaults to the FIRST occurrence ever, so adding a term mid-tenancy back-bills every past period; the picker only offers the first 18 occurrences
description: startOptions is `occurrences.slice(0, 18)` (PaymentsPage.tsx:486, and again at :439) over the tenancy's occurrences sorted by due_date ASCENDING — i.e. the EARLIEST 18, all of them in the past for any schedule older than 18 periods. UtilityCard defaults startsOnSequence to `term?.starts_on_sequence ?? startOptions[0]?.sequenceNo ?? 1` (PaymentsPage.tsx:125), and AddAdditionalPaymentDialog does the same (AddAdditionalPaymentDialog.tsx:75) — i.e. the very first occurrence of the schedule. materialize_due_charges()'s term loop has no lower bound tied to when the term was created: it matches every occurrence with `due_date <= current_date and sequence_no >= term.starts_on_sequence and mod(sequence_no - starts_on_sequence, frequency_months) = 0` (20260715011000.sql:59-66). So the moment a fixed term is saved, the DB back-fills a charge for every past period.
failure_scenario: Tenancy started billing 2026-01-05 (seq 1). On 2026-07-14 the owner adds a 'ועד בית' fixed term of ₪150/month. The 'מתחיל מ־' select defaults to option[0] = 5 בינואר 2026 (sequence_no 1). saveBillingSettings/updateAdditionalPayment call materializeDueCharges(), which immediately inserts committee charges for occurrences 1-7 (Jan…Jul) — ₪1,050 of retroactive debt that the tenant was never told about — and PaymentsPage's totalDue jumps by ₪1,050. Worse, on a tenancy older than 18 periods the dropdown contains ONLY past dates (the first 18 occurrences), so the owner literally cannot choose 'start from the current period' — every possible choice back-bills.
suggested_fix: Build startOptions from the current occurrence forward (e.g. occurrences.filter(o => o.due_date >= today).slice(0, 18), plus a few recent ones), and default startsOnSequence to the CURRENT occurrence's sequence_no rather than occurrences[0]. Optionally bound materialize_due_charges' term loop by `occurrence.due_date >= term.created_at::date` unless the owner explicitly opted into a back-dated start.

title: "Today" is computed in UTC while the owner is in Asia/Jerusalem — between 00:00 and 03:00 local, a meter reading is written onto the PREVIOUS period's charge, overwriting a paid charge's amount and readings
description: Every 'today' in the billing client is `new Date().toISOString().slice(0,10)` — i.e. the UTC date (src/api/billing.ts:18, src/hooks/useBilling.ts:88, :108, :180, src/components/PaymentsPage.tsx:431 and :479, src/components/PaymentHistoryDialog.tsx:45). The DB is UTC too (verified live: TimeZone=UTC, db_now 2026-07-14 22:23 UTC while the owner's local clock reads 2026-07-15 01:23 IDT, and current_date = 2026-07-14). Israel is UTC+3 (IDT) / UTC+2 (IST), so for the first 2-3 hours of every local day the app's 'today' is YESTERDAY. scheduledPeriod (useBilling.ts:107-126) picks `due[due.length-1]` = the last occurrence with due_date <= todayUTC; on the morning of a due date that occurrence is excluded, so it silently returns the PREVIOUS period. ensureCharge (useBilling.ts:330) then upserts on (owner_id, tenancy_id, payment_type, period_key) — which is the previous period's key — so it OVERWRITES that charge's amount_due, meter_previous, meter_current and meter_rate. (PaymentEditorDialog.tsx:17-19 is the only place that computes a LOCAL date, so paid_at and the due-date logic also disagree about which day it is.)
failure_scenario: Occurrence due 2026-07-15; owner opens the app at 01:20 on 2026-07-15 Israel time (= 2026-07-14 22:20 UTC, exactly the state observed live). todayISO() = '2026-07-14', so the 2026-07-15 occurrence is not 'due' and scheduledPeriod returns the 2026-06-15 occurrence. Owner enters the electricity meter reading for July (₪240). saveUtilityCharge builds periodKey = `term:<id>:schedule:gregorian:2026-06-15` and ensureCharge upserts — conflicting with June's existing electricity charge, which was ₪180 and already fully paid. June's charge is rewritten to ₪240 with July's meter_previous/meter_current, its payment history now shows a partially-paid ₪240 bill, and July's electricity charge is never created. Also, in that window PaymentsPage's dueCharges (line 431-435) excludes every charge due today, understating לתשלום by a full period.
suggested_fix: Use a single local-date helper (e.g. the toLocaleDateString('sv-SE') / getFullYear+getMonth+getDate form already used in PaymentEditorDialog) everywhere 'today' is compared against a `date` column, and set the Postgres session/db timezone to 'Asia/Jerusalem' (or use `(now() at time zone 'Asia/Jerusalem')::date` instead of current_date) in materialize_due_charges and save_tenancy_billing_schedule.

title: Electricity/water and meter-term cards never show the remaining balance on a partial payment
description: The owner's stated #1 requirement is that a partially paid debt stays visible. The rent card (line 562) and FixedTermRow (line 869) do render '₪X מתוך ₪Y'. UtilityCard — the card used for חשמל and מים, i.e. the two payment types the owner touches most — renders only `₪{currentCharge.amount_due}` (line 180) plus a 'חלקי' badge. The paid amount and the remaining amount appear nowhere on the card. Worse, the summary line at line 306 prints `לתשלום: ₪{calculatedAmount}` where calculatedAmount is derived from the meter inputs (i.e. the FULL charge), so on a partially paid charge the card literally says 'לתשלום: ₪320' when only ₪120 is actually owed. MeterTermRow has the same hole (line 781 shows the recomputed full amount, no paid/remaining anywhere).
failure_scenario: Electricity charge for דירה 3 is ₪320. Tenant pays ₪200 in cash; owner records it via 'ערוך' → שולם עד עכשיו = 200. Back on the payments screen the חשמל card shows '₪320', a grey 'חלקי' badge, and 'לתשלום: ₪320'. The ₪120 still owed is displayed nowhere on the card — the owner has to open היסטוריה וחובות (a different dialog) or do the subtraction himself, and the card's own 'לתשלום' line states the wrong number.
suggested_fix: In UtilityCard/MeterTermRow show `שולם ₪{paid} מתוך ₪{due}` and, when paid > 0 and paid < due, `נשאר ₪{due - paid}`; and stop labelling the input-derived preview 'לתשלום' when a charge already exists with payments against it.

title: UtilityCard wipes half-typed meter readings on every parent re-render (unstable `startOptions` array in useEffect deps)
description: UtilityCard's reset effect (lines 119-129) lists `startOptions` in its dependency array. `startOptions` is rebuilt with `.map()` inside the tenancy loop on every PaymentsPage render (line 486) and handed to the card through `utilityData()` (line 535), so it is a NEW array identity on every render of PaymentsPage. Object.is therefore never matches, and the effect re-runs on EVERY parent render — not only when the charge/term actually changes. The effect calls setPreviousReading / setCurrentReading / setUnitRate / setFixedAmount / setCalculationType / setFrequencyMonths / setStartsOnSequence, so it overwrites whatever the user has typed with the values from the (possibly nonexistent) saved term. PaymentsPage re-renders on any of its own state changes (setHistoryOpen, setAddingFor, setEditingRent, setEditingCharge, setTermToDelete...) and on every `pendingKeys` change from Index (useBilling sets a new Set at the start and end of every mutation, useBilling.ts:136/150). This is exactly the screen the owner said must be the easiest place to enter a meter reading. Same unstable-deps pattern exists in AddAdditionalPaymentDialog (deps `[initialTerm, open, startOptions]`, line 77) and UtilitySettingsDialog (deps `[open, startOptions, term]`, line 926), where `startOptionsForTenancy()` also returns a fresh array each render (lines 645/654/675) — those forms reset themselves while open if the parent re-renders.
failure_scenario: Owner opens תשלומים. In the חשמל card for דירה 3 he types מונה אחרון=1200, מונה נוכחי=1350, מחיר ליחידה=0.62 (the 'לתשלום' line correctly previews ₪93). Before pressing 'חשב תשלום' he clicks 'סמן שולם' on that tenancy's rent (or on any other card, or opens 'היסטוריה וחובות', or 'הוסף תשלום נוסף'). That state change re-renders PaymentsPage → new `startOptions` identity → UtilityCard's effect fires → currentReading is set back to '' , previousReading back to the old stored reading, unitRate back to the term rate, and the calculation-type toggle flips back to the term's mode. The three numbers the owner just walked down to the meter to read are gone, silently, with no warning and no way to recover them.
suggested_fix: Memoize `startOptions` (useMemo keyed on the occurrences array + calendar) or drop it from the dependency arrays and key the reset on stable ids (`term?.id`, `currentCharge?.id`) instead.

title: Lowering a charge's amount silently DELETES the record of money already received
description: saveUtilityCharge (line 342), saveMeterTermCharge (line 485) and saveFixedTermCharge (line 517) all do: ensureCharge() upserts the charge with the NEW (lower) amount_due, then, if the cached charge shows paid_amount > new amount, they call setChargePaymentState(charge_id, amount_due=new, paid_amount=new) to 'clamp'. set_charge_payment_state (live DB, verified via pg_get_functiondef) implements a payment change by DELETING every payment_allocations row for the charge and DELETING/decrementing the parent payments row, then inserting one fresh payment for the new amount. So the clamp does not carry the excess anywhere — it erases it. There is no credit, no overpayment row, no note, no audit trail. The ledger now claims the tenant paid less than they actually did.
failure_scenario: Electricity meter, term rate 2.70. Owner mistypes the current reading as 5500 instead of 550 -> charge amount_due = (5500-50)*2.70 = 14,715. Tenant is billed and actually pays 14,715 (owner clicks 'סמן שולם'; payments row = 14,715, allocation = 14,715). Owner notices the typo, re-enters the reading as 550 and clicks 'עדכן חיוב'. ensureCharge rewrites amount_due to 1,350; the guard fires (14,715 > 1,350) and setChargePaymentState deletes the 14,715 payment + allocation and inserts a single 1,350 payment. The 13,365 the tenant actually transferred no longer exists anywhere in charges, payments or payment_allocations. The history dialog and the 'שולם' total silently drop by 13,365 and the tenant is owed a refund the system has no record of.
suggested_fix: Never let a charge-amount edit rewrite the payment ledger. Reduce amount_due only, leave allocations intact, and represent paid > due as an explicit credit/overpayment (or refuse the edit and require the owner to reverse the payment first). At minimum, do it in one SECURITY-checked RPC that records a reversal row instead of DELETE-ing payments.

title: listCharges() is unpaginated — PostgREST silently truncates and the OLDEST arrears disappear from the totals
description: listCharges selects every charge with no .limit()/.range() and no count check, ordered by due_date DESC. Supabase's PostgREST enforces a max-rows cap (default 1,000) and truncates the result set without any error. Charges accumulate at (1 rent + N terms) per occurrence per tenancy, and save_tenancy_billing_schedule generates 48 occurrences per tenancy, so the cap is reachable for a normal multi-unit landlord. Because the ordering is due_date DESC, the rows dropped are the oldest — exactly the unpaid arrears the history screen exists to surface. Both the PaymentsPage summary tiles (PaymentsPage.tsx:434-435) and PaymentHistoryDialog totals (PaymentHistoryDialog.tsx:52-56) are reduce() over this truncated array.
failure_scenario: Owner with 6 active tenancies, each with rent + electricity + water + ועד בית, after 4 years of monthly occurrences has ~1,150 charges. listCharges returns only the newest 1,000. The ~150 oldest charges — including a ₪3,000 rent charge from month 2 that was never paid — are absent from `charges`, so PaymentHistoryDialog (even with 'הצג רק פתוחים') never lists them and the 'נשאר' tile under-reports the tenant's outstanding debt by ₪3,000. Nothing errors; the owner believes the tenant is square.
suggested_fix: Paginate (or aggregate paid_amount server-side in a view / RPC and select with an explicit range), and assert the returned count against a head-count so truncation can never pass unnoticed.

title: A failed billing query renders as 'nothing is paid' — no error state anywhere on the payments screen
description: All four billing queries (charges at 46-53, payment terms 55-59, settings 61-65, occurrences 67-71) destructure only `data` and `isLoading`; `isError`/`error` are never read, and nothing toasts on query failure. Mutations toast via runForTenancy, but reads do not. PaymentsPage only has a loading branch (line 446) and no error branch. On query failure React Query leaves `data` undefined → the defaults `= []` kick in → isLoading is false → the page renders as if the owner simply has no charges. Note the charges queryFn also calls `materializeDueCharges()` first (line 49), so an RPC failure (e.g. the auth/authorization errors that function raises) takes the whole charge list down with it.
failure_scenario: The session token has expired / the network drops / materialize_due_charges() raises. React Query retries, gives up, sets status=error. The owner sees no toast and no error text: the totals bar reads לתשלום ₪0 / שולם ₪0 / נשאר ₪0, every rent card shows a red 'לא שולם' with '₪0 מתוך ₪5,000', every utility card shows 'לא שולם', and היסטוריה וחובות says 'אין חיובים להצגה'. A failed read is indistinguishable from 'the tenant paid nothing and all my payment history is gone' — a dead end with no instruction to retry.
suggested_fix: Read `isError`/`error` from the queries, surface a toast.error + an in-page error state with a retry button, and do not let PaymentsPage render the 'everything unpaid' view when a read failed.

title: 'חשב מחדש' on a paid charge silently reduces/destroys the recorded payment — no confirmation, success toast
description: The 'חשב מחדש' button in UtilityCard (line 317), MeterTermRow (line 797) and FixedTermRow (line 874) stays enabled after a charge is fully paid — only 'סמן שולם' is disabled. When the recomputed amount is lower than what was already paid, saveUtilityCharge (useBilling.ts:342-348), saveMeterTermCharge (485-491) and saveFixedTermCharge (517-523) call setChargePaymentState with paid_amount = the new (lower) amount. That RPC deletes the existing payment_allocations and the payments rows and re-inserts a smaller payment. The UI asks for no confirmation and then shows a green success toast ('חיוב חשמל חושב ונשמר'). PaymentEditorDialog has the same hole from the other direction: typing 0 into 'שולם עד עכשיו' and saving deletes the payment record with no confirm and a 'התשלום עודכן' success toast.
failure_scenario: Electricity charge for July is ₪400 and the tenant paid all ₪400 (badge: שולם). The owner notices he typed the meter reading with an extra digit; the correct reading yields ₪250. He fixes the reading and clicks 'חשב מחדש'. Without any prompt the ₪400 payment row is deleted and replaced by a ₪250 payment; the ₪150 the tenant actually handed over is erased from the ledger and from the 'שולם' totals, and the toast says the operation succeeded.
suggested_fix: Before recomputing a charge whose paid_amount exceeds the new amount, show an AlertDialog stating the recorded payment of ₪X will be reduced to ₪Y (or that the credit must be handled separately), and require explicit confirmation. Same for zeroing 'שולם עד עכשיו' in PaymentEditorDialog.

title: The 48-occurrence horizon is generated once and never extended — billing silently stops for tenancies that outlive it
description: Both places that write a schedule hard-code `count: 48` (useBilling.ts:165 for saveBillingSettings and useBilling.ts:195 for ensureDefaultSchedules), and ensureDefaultSchedules only ever fires for tenancies that have NO tenancy_billing_settings row (useBilling.ts:181-184), so it never re-runs. Nothing anywhere extends or tops up billing_schedule_occurrences. materialize_due_charges() creates charges exclusively from occurrence rows, so once the 48 occurrences are exhausted the tenancy stops being billed with no error, no toast and no visual cue. The DB even allows 72 (migration line 104) but the client never uses it.
failure_scenario: Owner adds a long-term tenancy on 2026-07-14; ensureDefaultSchedules writes 48 monthly occurrences 2026-07-14 … 2030-06-01. The tenant stays. On 2030-07-01 there is no occurrence, so the cron creates no rent charge. currentOccurrenceByTenancyId (useBilling.ts:87-95) keeps returning the last past occurrence, so PaymentsPage keeps rendering 'מועד חיוב: 1 ביוני 2030' forever and the utility cards keep pointing at the June-2030 period_key. Rent for July 2030 onward is never billed and the owner is given no indication that the schedule ran out.
suggested_fix: Top the schedule up: on each load (or inside materialize_due_charges) ensure at least N future occurrences exist for every active tenancy, appending from the last sequence_no. Or bound the schedule by tenancy.end_date and raise/warn when the generated window ends before it.

title: period_key is the due DATE, not the period — changing due_day double-bills the current month
description: period_key is built as `schedule:gregorian:${iso}` / `schedule:hebrew:${iso}` (billingSchedule.ts:196 and :233), i.e. it encodes the exact due date. The rent charge key is therefore `rent:schedule:gregorian:<due-date>` (migration line 22/49 of 20260715011000). It is unique, but it is NOT stable: the same calendar month gets a DIFFERENT period_key when due_day changes. Combined with the DELETE cutting at `due_date >= current_date` (which leaves the current month's already-materialized occurrence in place when its old due date is in the past), a due_day change inserts a SECOND occurrence for the same month with a new key, and `on conflict (owner_id, tenancy_id, payment_type, period_key) do nothing` cannot dedupe it because the key differs. There is also no unique constraint on (owner_id, tenancy_id, sequence_no) (verified against the live DB), so the same sequence_no legitimately ends up on two rows.
failure_scenario: Tenancy: rent ₪5,000, gregorian, due_day 5. On 2026-07-05 the cron materializes charge `rent:schedule:gregorian:2026-07-05`, ₪5,000. Tenant pays it in full on 2026-07-08. On 2026-07-14 the owner changes יום בחודש from 5 to 25. RPC: DELETE (due_date >= 2026-07-14) does not touch 2026-07-05; INSERT adds 2026-07-25 (seq 7) — so 2026-07 now has TWO occurrences, both with sequence_no 7. On 2026-07-25 the cron inserts `rent:schedule:gregorian:2026-07-25`, ₪5,000, a brand-new unpaid rent charge. The tenant is now shown as owing ₪5,000 for a July they already paid; totalDue on PaymentsPage is inflated by a full month's rent and PaymentHistoryDialog lists two July rent rows. Same mechanism duplicates every fixed term charge for that month.
suggested_fix: Make period_key identify the PERIOD, not the due date — e.g. `schedule:gregorian:2026-07` and `schedule:hebrew:5786:Av` (both Adars already produce distinct month names via the en-u-ca-hebrew formatter, so 'Adar I'/'Adar II' keys are safe). Then a due_day change UPDATEs the existing occurrence's due_date under the same key, ON CONFLICT dedupes correctly, and no month can be billed twice or skipped.

title: ensureDefaultSchedules can silently overwrite a saved billing schedule with defaults because it runs before the billing-settings query has loaded
description: ensureDefaultSchedules (useBilling.ts:178-213) decides which tenancies need a default schedule from `billingSettingsByTenancyId` (derived from the ['billing-settings', user?.id] query) with the only guard being `if (!user) return`. There is NO guard for the settings query still loading (no areSettingsLoading / enabled check). Index.tsx:60-62 calls it unconditionally in a useEffect keyed on activeByUnitId. On a cold load the ['billing-settings'] query and the tenancies query (source of activeByUnitId) fire in parallel and resolve in nondeterministic order. If tenancies resolves first, billingSettingsByTenancyId is still empty ([]), so EVERY active tenancy is classified as `missing` and gets saveTenancyBillingSchedule({calendar:'gregorian', dueDay:1, startDate:today}) called on it. The DB function save_tenancy_billing_schedule (migration 20260714213000, lines 114-124) upserts with `on conflict (tenancy_id) do update set calendar_type=..., due_day=..., schedule_start_date=...` and then `delete from billing_schedule_occurrences where due_date >= current_date` and regenerates them — i.e. it unconditionally overwrites any existing schedule and regenerates future occurrence period_keys. The per-session defaultScheduleIdsRef guard does not help: the damaging first call has already fired with the empty (stale) settings before the settings query resolves.
failure_scenario: 1) Landlord earlier saved tenancy T's schedule as Hebrew calendar, due day 15 (rows in tenancy_billing_settings + billing_schedule_occurrences with Hebrew period_keys; rent charges materialized against them, current month already marked paid). 2) Landlord reloads the app (React Query cache empty). 3) The tenancies query resolves before ['billing-settings'], so activeByUnitId is populated while billingSettings is still []. 4) The Index effect calls ensureDefaultSchedules; T is in `missing` (billingSettingsByTenancyId.has(T.id)===false). 5) saveTenancyBillingSchedule runs with gregorian/day-1/today. 6) save_tenancy_billing_schedule overwrites T's settings to gregorian/day-1 and deletes+regenerates future occurrences with new Gregorian period_keys. Outcome: the saved Hebrew day-15 schedule is silently reverted to Gregorian day 1; the already-paid current-month rent charge (keyed on the old occurrence period_key) no longer matches any occurrence so the UI shows it as missing/unpaid, and materialize_due_charges inserts a duplicate rent charge under the new period_key.
suggested_fix: Do not run ensureDefaultSchedules until the billing-settings (and occurrences) queries have finished loading. E.g. pass areSettingsLoading/areOccurrencesLoading into the guard (return early while loading), or gate the Index useEffect on `!billingLoading`, so `missing` is only computed against fully-loaded settings.

title: New payment terms default to the earliest occurrence and instantly back-fill retroactive debt
description: The 'מתחיל מ־' select defaults to startOptions[0].sequenceNo — occurrence #1 of the tenancy's schedule, which for any tenancy older than a month is a date in the past (PaymentsPage.tsx:486 builds startOptions from the full occurrence list, oldest first). addAdditionalPayment creates the term, and the very next billing query runs materialize_due_charges(), whose fixed-term INSERT matches every occurrence with due_date <= current_date and sequence_no >= starts_on_sequence. So a term created today immediately produces one unpaid charge for every past occurrence, all at today's fixed_amount. The same happens via updateUtilityPaymentSettings when a meter utility is switched to 'מחיר קבוע'.
failure_scenario: Tenancy started 2026-01-01 with a 48-occurrence schedule. On 2026-11-20 the owner adds a 'ועד בית' term at ₪300/month and leaves 'מתחיל מ־' at its default (the January occurrence). materialize_due_charges immediately inserts 11 charges (Jan–Nov) of ₪300 each, all paid_amount 0. The tenant instantly owes ₪3,300 of committee fees for months that were never billed and were settled outside the app; totalDue and the history dialog both show the phantom debt.
suggested_fix: Default 'מתחיל מ־' to the first occurrence with due_date >= today, and/or have materialize_due_charges only create charges for occurrences on or after the term's created_at.

title: set_charge_payment_state overwrites the payment ledger instead of appending — installment dates and amounts are lost
description: Every payment write in the app goes through set_charge_payment_state, whose body deletes all payment_allocations for the charge and deletes/decrements the parent payments rows before inserting one new payment for the cumulative total. payments is therefore not a ledger — it holds at most one synthetic row per charge, always re-dated and re-noted ('עודכן ממסך סקירה'). markChargePaid (useBilling.ts:527) does not even pass paid_at, so the RPC's CURRENT_DATE default is used and any earlier payment date is overwritten with today. Balances stay arithmetically consistent, but the record of when and in how many installments the money arrived is destroyed on every edit, and a mis-typed 0 in the editor deletes the payment record with no confirmation and no undo.
failure_scenario: Rent charge ₪3,000. Tenant pays ₪1,000 on 2026-07-05; owner records it (payments row: amount 1000, paid_at 2026-07-05). Tenant pays the remaining ₪2,000 on 2026-07-25; owner opens the editor, sets 'שולם עד עכשיו' = 3000, date 2026-07-25 and saves. The 2026-07-05 payment row is DELETEd and replaced by a single payments row (3000, 2026-07-25). The database now says the whole ₪3,000 arrived on the 25th; the ₪1,000 received on the 5th is unrecoverable, so late-fee/receipt evidence for the first installment no longer exists.
suggested_fix: Make payments append-only: record each installment as its own payments + payment_allocations row (with its own paid_at), and expose an explicit 'reverse/delete this payment' action instead of recomputing the cumulative state by deletion.

title: tests/billing.test.ts has no anonymous-client assertion, so the anon EXECUTE grant on the SECURITY DEFINER RPCs is invisible to the suite
description: Every client in the billing suite is authenticated: beforeAll (lines 13-15) builds `alice` and `bob` via signInAs(), and there is no third client created from the anon key with no session. The cross-owner tests are sound (they assert on RPCs that raise, and the one RLS-denial assertion at line 152 checks the returned row set is empty, which would flip to a non-empty array if the policy were loosened). But nothing in the suite ever calls an RPC as an unauthenticated caller, and nothing asserts on the anon role's EXECUTE privilege. That is precisely why the ineffective `revoke ... from public` in both migrations shipped unnoticed and why the pg_cron/anon path in known bug (a) went undetected: the tests can only see authenticated callers. There is also no test that Bob cannot call save_tenancy_billing_schedule with Alice's tenancy_id, even though that is the only SECURITY DEFINER function in phase 2 that takes a caller-supplied tenancy id.
failure_scenario: Run the whole billing suite against the live database today. It passes green, while has_function_privilege('anon', 'public.materialize_due_charges()', 'EXECUTE') is TRUE and an unauthenticated curl to /rest/v1/rpc/materialize_due_charges executes as SECURITY DEFINER. A green suite therefore certifies a database in which anonymous callers can invoke privileged RPCs.
suggested_fix: Add an anon client (createClient with the publishable key and no signIn) and assert that .rpc('materialize_due_charges'), .rpc('save_tenancy_billing_schedule', ...), .rpc('set_charge_payment_state', ...) and .rpc('delete_added_payment_term', ...) all return a non-null error. Add a Bob-calls-save_tenancy_billing_schedule-with-Alice's-tenancy_id test asserting error is non-null AND that Alice's billing_schedule_occurrences rows for that tenancy are unchanged.

title: RTL bug: calendar icon overlaps the date value in PaymentEditorDialog (physical `right-3` vs logical `pe-10` on a dir=rtl input)
description: The CalendarDays icon is absolutely positioned with the PHYSICAL class `right-3` (line 152) while the input it decorates carries `dir="rtl"` and the LOGICAL class `pe-10` (line 158-159). With dir=rtl, `padding-inline-end` resolves to padding-LEFT, and Tailwind emits `pe-*` after the Input's base `px-3` (src/components/ui/input.tsx:11), so the field ends up with padding-left: 2.5rem and padding-right: 0.75rem. The reserved space is on the wrong side: the icon sits at the right edge, directly on top of where an RTL date input starts rendering its day/month/year fields. Contrast the two ₪ fields in the same dialog (lines 113/132), which work only because those inputs are `dir="ltr"`, making pe-8 resolve to padding-right and match the `right-3` span. This is the exact physical-vs-logical mix the phase-1 fix was supposed to eliminate.
failure_scenario: Owner opens 'ערוך' on a rent charge to record a partial payment. The תאריך התשלום field renders its date directly underneath the calendar glyph at the right edge — the first date segment is obscured/unreadable and clicking there hits the pointer-events-none icon area rather than the segment — while 2.5rem of empty padding sits unused on the left.
suggested_fix: Use `start-3` (or `end-3` with matching `ps-10`) for the icon and keep the padding utility on the same logical side as the icon; do not mix `right-*` with `pe-*` on a dir=rtl input.

title: Utility cards show a red 'לא שולם' badge when no charge exists at all
description: `paymentState(undefined)` returns 'unpaid' (line 52), and PaymentBadge maps 'unpaid' to the destructive (red) variant with the text 'לא שולם'. UtilityCard passes `currentCharge` straight through, and `currentCharge` is undefined until the owner has actually calculated a חשמל/מים charge for the current occurrence. So a card with no bill at all is rendered identically to a card with an unpaid debt. FixedTermRow at least prints the clarifying 'עדיין לא נוצר חיוב למועד הזה' (line 869); UtilityCard prints nothing.
failure_scenario: Owner creates a new tenancy for דירה 5. He opens תשלומים: the חשמל and מים cards both display a red 'לא שולם' badge even though he has not entered a single meter reading and the tenant owes nothing for utilities. Every new unit starts life looking like it is in arrears on two payment types.
suggested_fix: Render a neutral/outline badge ('טרם חושב') when charge is undefined, and reserve the destructive 'לא שולם' badge for a charge that exists with paid_amount = 0.

title: saveCurrentRentPayment reads input.frequencyMonths / input.startsOnSequence, which are not on its parameter type
description: saveCurrentRentPayment's input type (useBilling.ts:246-251) is only { tenancy, amountDue, paidAmount, paidAt }, but line 253 calls scheduledPeriod(input.tenancy.id, input.frequencyMonths, input.startsOnSequence). Those two properties do not exist on the type (confirmed: `tsc -p tsconfig.app.json` reports TS2339 at 253:65 and 253:88), so this breaks the type-checked build (`npm run build`). At runtime under the Vite/esbuild dev server the accesses evaluate to undefined and scheduledPeriod's default parameters (frequencyMonths=1, startsOnSequence=1) take over, which happens to be correct for monthly rent — so behavior is currently harmless, but it is a dead/incorrect reference and it fails the production type-check.
failure_scenario: Run the production build step (`tsc -p tsconfig.app.json --noEmit`): it exits non-zero with `error TS2339: Property 'frequencyMonths' does not exist ...` and `Property 'startsOnSequence' does not exist ...` at useBilling.ts line 253, blocking the build. (At runtime the rent editor still works because scheduledPeriod's default params supply 1/1.)
suggested_fix: Remove the two arguments (call scheduledPeriod(input.tenancy.id)) since rent is monthly and the defaults already apply, or add frequencyMonths/startsOnSequence to the input type and have the rent editor supply them.

title: Type error in saveCurrentRentPayment; plan's "TypeScript passes" is a false pass
description: saveCurrentRentPayment reads input.frequencyMonths and input.startsOnSequence (line 253) but its input type only declares { tenancy, amountDue, paidAmount, paidAt } (lines 246-251). The real project type check `tsc -b --noEmit` fails with two TS2339 errors here (verified). The plan (Task P7) claims TypeScript passes, but the verification command it lists, bare `tsc --noEmit`, exits 0 because the root tsconfig.json uses project references with no direct files — it checks nothing. The production build survives only because `vite build` (package.json) uses esbuild and does not type-check. Runtime is harmless: both values are undefined, so scheduledPeriod falls back to its (1,1) defaults, which is correct for monthly rent. The finding is the broken type safety and the misleading verification, not a runtime bug.
failure_scenario: Run `npm run build`-adjacent typecheck `npx tsc -b`: it errors with TS2339 on useBilling.ts:253, so any CI gate or IDE that runs the real project typecheck is red, while the plan asserts green. No runtime misbehavior for rent.
suggested_fix: Either drop the two extra args in the scheduledPeriod(input.tenancy.id) call (rent is always monthly) or add frequencyMonths/startsOnSequence to the input type, and change the plan's verification to `tsc -b`.
